Integrative Biology Seminar - Lillian Aoki, Assistant Professor

Oregon State University Events

Structure, function, and extreme events in coastal vegetated habitats Lillian Aoki is a coastal scientist studying ecosystem dynamics and resilience in nearshore and estuarine habitats. She uses a variety of field, lab, and computational methods to build an integrated and cross-scale understanding of coastal ecology in a rapidly changing world. Current projects focus on understanding recovery trajectories of seagrass meadows following marine heatwaves and the role of land management in facilitating carbon sequestration in tidal marshes. She earned her PhD in Environmental Sciences from the University of Virginia. For more information about Lilian, please go to https://coasts.uoregon.edu/peop

announcedLaw & Civic

Ten for Teaching: Instituting flexible course policies that support all learners (ASYNCHRONOUS)

Boise State University Events

During the COVID-19 pandemic many educators loosened their course policies (e.g., around attendance and late work). Several years later, some of that flexibility has remained, with educators noting both positive and negative impacts on student learning. This dichotomy leads many of us to wonder what the right balance of flexibility is. In this workshop, we will begin by exploring the demographics of Boise State students and how those might impact the choices we make. In addition, you will have the opportunity to discuss your thoughts and assumptions about course policies, review different policy models, and consider what policies best support your students' learning. In this presentation I will review Australian and international evidence on health outcomes and health service use among justice-involved people, and consider how to leverage this evidence to reduce health inequities in a highly politicised, socially-excluded population. Course Design for Large Enrolment Classes: Turning Exams into Learning Using Two-stage Exams

Centre for Teaching, Learning and Technology

Midterm and final exams are high-stakes evaluation events that can be stressful for many students. Changes in the exam structure may turn exams into valuable opportunities for peer learning through discussion and feedback. In this one-hour workshop, guest faculty facilitators will discuss how they adapted this assessment approach for large classes, including exam design, classroom logistics, practical considerations for implementation, student feedback, and lesson learned.
